Prepare Documents for Online Forms

Online forms often reject files because the format, dimensions, page order, or file size is wrong. This workflow combines the most useful FreeToolCo tools for application, exam, job, and document-upload portals.

Recommended workflow

  1. Resize or compress photos before upload.
  2. Resize signature images to the required dimensions.
  3. Convert JPG/PNG documents into a PDF when the portal asks for PDF.
  4. Merge multiple PDFs into the exact required order.
  5. Check the final file before submitting the form.

Tools used in this workflow

  • Compress Image to 20KB — Compress JPG, PNG, or WebP images to around 20KB for online forms, exams, and document uploads.
  • Compress Image to 50KB — Reduce image size to around 50KB online for applications, profile uploads, and mobile-friendly sharing.
  • Passport Photo Resizer — Resize photos to common passport and application dimensions such as 3.5cm x 4.5cm, 200x200, and 600x600 pixels.
  • Signature Resizer — Resize signature images for online forms and applications. Set width, height, and target KB size in your browser.
  • JPG to PDF Converter — Convert JPG images into a clean PDF online for free. Arrange images, choose page size, set margins, and download instantly with no signup.
  • Merge PDF — Merge multiple PDF files into one PDF online for free. Reorder files, combine documents, and download one clean PDF without signup.
  • Compress PDF — Optimize PDF files online with a browser-based re-save tool. Shows before/after size and clearly reports when a PDF is already optimized.

Why this workflow works

It follows a safe order: fix dimensions and format first, then optimize size, then verify the final output. This prevents quality loss and reduces repeated uploads.

Frequently asked questions

Can this guarantee a portal will accept my file?

No. Every portal has its own rules. Use the workflow to match the stated format, size, and dimensions as closely as possible.

Should I resize or compress first?

Resize first when dimensions are too large, then compress if there is still a KB limit.
